options.text: Plant P is a shrub — many hard woody stems branch close to the ground.
Plant Q is a tree — one main thick woody trunk with branches high above the ground.
Plant P is a herb — it is shorter than a tree.
Plant Q is a climber — woody stems mean it needs support.

stem:
Anika studies two garden plants.
Plant P is shorter than a tree and has many hard brown woody stems that branch close to the ground.
Plant Q is a tall plant with one main thick woody trunk and branches high above the ground.

Which claims classify the plants correctly? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: A shrub has several hard woody stems branching near the ground. A tree has one main thick trunk with high branches. Shortness alone does not make a herb, and woody stems alone do not make a climber.
